la:noun:auxilium.html:
auxĭlĭum, ii, n.
augeo
,
help, aid, assistance, support, succor (syn.: adjumentum, opes, praesidium, subsidium).
In gen.: Fer mi auxilium, Enn. ap. : quo praesidio fretus, auxiliis quibus? Pac. ap. : auxilium argentarium,; : non habeo ad auxilium copiam,: navita indigus omni vitali auxilio,: venerunt ad auxilium,; —Hence the phrases: auxilium esse alicui,to assist one,; and more freq.: auxilio esse alicui, Enn. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; : auxilium ferre alicui,to bring assistance, to aid, succor,; ; ; ; ; (contra aliquem),; ; ; ; ; ; ; ib. Job, 30, 13 al.; once adferre,: dare,; ; : praebere,; : auxilium sibi adjungere,: expetere,: unde auxilium petam?: petere ab aliquo,; ; ; ; Esdr. 8, 22; ib. Judith, 6, 21 et saep.—In plur.: cum (mare) tumet, auxiliis adsidet ille (navita) suis,: auxilia portare, Kritz: magna duo auxilia,sources of aid,: ne auxilia liberorum innocentibus deessent, et saep.—Meton. (abstr. for concr.), a place of succor, refuge (eccl. Lat.): sex (oppida) erunt in fugitivorum auxilia separata,. —
Esp.
In milit. lang. very freq., and commonly in plur.: auxĭlĭa, ōrum, auxiliary troops, auxiliaries (mostly composed of allies and light-armed troops; hence opp. to the legions): auxilium appellatum ab auctu, cum accesserant ei qui adjumento essent alienigenae, Müll.; ; cf. auxiliares, and Smith, Dict. Antiq.: quibus (copiis) rex Deiotarus imperatoribus nostris auxilia mitteret,; so ; : auxiliis in mediam aciem conjectis,; so, dimittere,: ab sociis et nomine Latino accersere,; cf. : facere mercede,; ; et saep.—Opp to the legions: sex legiones et magna equitum ac peditum auxilia,; so ; ; ; ; ; ; —In sing.: Oroden auctus auxilio Pharasmanes vocare ad pugnam,; .—Borrowed from miht. lang.: Duodecim deis plus quam in caelo

deorumst inmortalium Mihi nunc auxilio adjutores sunt, : Auxilia ac socios jam pacto foedere habebant,.—In gen.: auxilia, military force, power: Caesar confisus famā rerum gestarum, infirmis auxiliis proficisci non dubitaverat,; ; .—

In medic. lang., an antidote, remedy, in the most extended sense of the word: corporis,; so ; ; , n. 21 al.: adversae valetudinis,; .—
Auxilium as a personified existence, like Fides. Salus, etc., in .

la:verb:auxilio.gloss: to help, aid, assist; to be useful

la:adj:auxiliaris.html:
auxĭlĭāris (AVXSILIARIS, Inscr. Momm. 5778), e, adj.
auxilium
.
Bringing help or aid, aiding, helping, assisting, auxiliary (syn.: auxiliarius, opem ferens): undae,: Dea (sc. Lucina),: numen,: carmen,a formula of incantation in aid of Jason,; cf. : arma (poet. periphrastically for the prose auxilia; v.infra), auxiliaries, : aera, the cymbals, trumpets, kettles, etc., by rattling which the ancients believed that they were able to drive away an eclipse of the moon, : oleum auxiliare lethargicis,: auxiliaria fulmina, quae advocata seu advocantium bono veniunt,: auxiliares milites, cohortes, etc.; or absol.: auxĭlĭāres, ium, m., auxiliary troops, auxiliaries (freq. opp. legiones): auxiliares dicuntur in bello socii Romanorum exterarum nationum, Paul. ex Müll.: cohortes,; : equites,fin.: auxiliares,; ; ; ; Tac Agr. 18; ; and sing.: qui (Gannascus) auxiliaris et diu meritus Gallorum oram vastabat, Halm.—
Of or pertaining to auxiliaries: auxiliaria stipendia,.

la:noun:auxiliarius.html:
auxĭlĭārĭus (AVXSILIARIVS, Corp. Inscr. III. 4753), a, um, adj.
id.
,
bringing help, aiding, auxiliary (less freq. than the preceding): magis consiliarius amicus quam auxiliarius,.—In milit. lang.,
With milites, equites, cohors, auxiliary troops, auxiliaries (opp. legiones): miles, Asin. ap. : cohors,; ; Auct. B. Alex. 62; : equites,.—
Absol. (eccl. Lat.): assumpsit sibi auxiliarios,: fortes auxiliarii,.

la:verb:auxilior.gloss: to help, aid, assist; to be useful
senses: to help, aid, assist; to be useful
la:verb:auxilior.html:
auxĭlĭor, ātus, 1, v. dep.
auxilium
,
to give help or aid, to help, aid, assist, succor (syn.: juvo, adjuvo, opitulor, subvenio, succurro).
In gen. (class. but rare; in Cic. perh. only once in his Epistt.), constr. with dat.: alicui,: nonne id flagitiumst te aliis consilium dare, tibi non potis esse auxiliarier?; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; : nihil Numantinis vires corporis auxiliatae sunt, Auct. ad .—
Esp., of the aid of a physician, to aid, to relieve, heal, cure; constr. with dat. or contra: Nec (medicina) formidatis auxiliatur aquis,: ferulam quibusdam morbis auxiliari dicunt medici,: phalangites auxiliantur contra scorpionum ictus,.!*?
Act. access. form auxĭlĭo, āre, to give aid, etc.: alicui, Gracch. ap. P.; cf. P.—
Auxilior in pass. signif.: a me auxiliatus, Lucil. ap. Prisc. pp. 791 and 927 P.: consonantes sunt in quibus (vox) ab imis auxiliata egrediatur ad aures disertā verborum claritate,.

la:other:Auximum.gloss: a city in Picenum situated on a hill near Ancon, now the town of Osimo
senses: a city in Picenum situated on a hill near Ancon, now the town of Osimo
la:other:Auximum.html:
Auxĭmum, i, n.,
a town of the Piceni, now Osimo, ; ; ; .—Hence, Auxĭ-mātes, ium, m., the inhabitants of Auximum, ; ; cf. Mann. Ital. I. p. 489 sq.
